From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated slab sizing kickoff + attachments

Alex —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Attaching the traffic CSV you shared and an initial sizing workbook (dedicated_slab_proposal_v1.xlsx). High-level ask: we want to propose a committed Dedicated slab plan that meets your 95th percentile latency SLO (<= 500ms p95 for end-user responses) while keeping cost predictable and preserving a burst/fallback strategy for extreme spikes.

Quick summary of what we need from you to finalize numbers:
- Confirm whether the numbers in neurolytics_mvp_traffic.csv represent peak tokens/sec (burst) or 95th-percentile sustained windows.
- Callouts about multi-region failover (do you require active-active across two zones?)
- Any plan to change model quality/length assumptions during the pilot (avg generation tokens/per request).

What I attached:
- neurolytics_mvp_traffic.csv (your raw traffic export)
- dedicated_slab_proposal_v1.xlsx (working calc)
- draft_fallback_flow.pdf (conceptual fallback: model variant + degrade strategy)

Initial working assumptions I used in the sheet:
- Model: rw-13b-quant (production candidate)
- Observed per-GPU throughput (A100-like slab, quantized path): ~4,200 tokens/sec (measured at p95 latency ~= 450ms for 150-token outputs)
- Current CSV rows interpreted as: sustained 95th = 220,000 tokens/sec; short burst peak = 380,000 tokens/sec (please correct if wrong)

If those traffic numbers hold, the workbook shows very roughly:
- Sustained 95th: 220,000 tps -> base GPUs = ceil(220000 / 4200) = 53 GPUs
- Add 30% operational headroom: 53 * 1.3 = ~69 GPUs
- Burst peak (380k): ceil(380000 / 4200) = 91 GPUs -> with headroom ~119 GPUs

Proposed pattern in the workbook: commit to a 75-GPU slab (predictable cost + most expected sustained traffic covered), and configure a burst pool and/or hosted fallback that covers the top 10% of transient bursts to 380k. Also include a lower-quality model variant (rw-7b-quant) as an automated fallback to reduce GPU need by ~2x during spikes.

Can you confirm the CSV interpretation and whether a 500ms p95 SLO is the correct target? Once you confirm, we’ll finalize the workbook and run a short canary.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks, attaching the CSV we exported from our edge aggregator. Quick clarifications:
- The CSV column named 'window_95_tokens_per_sec' is our 95th-percentile sustained measured over 5-minute windows. That’s the 220k number you used.
- We also observed short bursts reported in 'instant_peak' rows up to ~380k tokens/sec, typically 10-30s spikes during peak load.
- We do want active-active across two AZs with automated failover; we expect cross-zone redundancy but prefer a single slab commitment if that reduces cost and we can rely on your routing/fallback.
- SLO: p95 user-facing latency <= 500ms is what we expect.

Would like you to call out per-AZ guaranteed capacity vs global burst capacity in the next revision. Also please surface the user-experience impact of falling back to rw-7b-quant (example prompt that fails gracefully).

Appreciate it — can you send updated numbers by EOD? We need to align with procurement next week.

—Alex

Alex — thanks for the quick clarifications. I updated the workbook and captured explicit per-AZ sizing and a fallback timeline. Summary of the revised recommended configuration (see dedicated_slab_proposal_v1.xlsx, tab "Recommended" for the formulas):

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model: rw-13b-quant
- Measured per-GPU throughput (p95 latency <= 500ms): 4,200 tokens/sec
- Sustained 95th (5-min windows): 220,000 tokens/sec
- Short burst peak (10-30s): 380,000 tokens/sec
- Headroom target: 30% operational (covers autoscale lag, cache warm, token-length variance)
- Cross-AZ target: Active-active routing; each AZ should be able to sustain ~60% of normal traffic if the other AZ is offline (operational requirement).

Raw calculations (explicit):
- Base GPUs required (sustained 95th): ceil(220,000 / 4,200) = 53 GPUs
- With 30% headroom: 53 * 1.3 = 68.9 -> round up = 69 GPUs
- Per-AZ split (active-active, target 60/40 if requested): AZ1 = 42 GPUs, AZ2 = 27 GPUs (total 69)
- Burst target (380k): ceil(380,000 / 4,200) = 91 GPUs -> headroom -> 91 * 1.3 = 118.3 -> round up = 119 GPUs

Recommended commercial configuration (what we propose you commit to):
1) Committed slab: 75 GPUs (single commitment covering majority of sustained load + baseline headroom). Rationale: simplifies billing and gives you room for modest growth without overcommit.
2) Burst pool: 50 GPUs (on-demand reserved burst reserved for short spikes). Combined committed + burst = 125 GPUs peak available.
3) Fallback flow: automated fallback to rw-7b-quant when burst > 100% of committed slab and queued requests exceed 10s, or p95 latency crosses 550ms for 1 minute. rw-7b-quant roughly doubles per-GPU throughput in our tests (conservative estimate), which reduces the peak GPU need by ~45-55% during fallback windows. See draft_fallback_flow.pdf for UX expectations and sample prompts and degraded output examples.

Risk notes:
- If your bursts become sustained beyond ~3 minutes, cost and degradation will increase; we recommend an alerting threshold at 2 minutes and a manual review policy.
- Cache warming: first few minutes of each major spike will see reduced effective throughput until KV cache warms; we account for that in the 30% headroom.

Next steps / action items:
- Alex: confirm acceptance of proposed 75-GPU slab + 50-GPU burst pool and the rw-7b automated fallback policy.
- Neurolytics SRE: confirm whether you require strict per-AZ minimums (we suggested 60/40 split) or if you accept cross-AZ routing without guaranteed per-AZ minimums.
- Redwood ops (Marissa / Laura): once Alex confirms, we’ll schedule a short canary (2-hour window) with pre-warmed cache and traffic replay.

I pasted the key calc cells below for visibility (you can cross-check in the workbook):
- per_gpu_tokens = 4200
- sustained_95 = 220000
- base_gpus = ceil(sustained_95 / per_gpu_tokens) = 53
- base_with_headroom = 69
- burst_gpus_with_headroom = 119

If that looks good, I’ll send an updated proposal for procurement and loop in legal for the Service Attachment that mentions burst policy.

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: dedicated_slab_proposal_v1.xlsx, draft_fallback_flow.pdf

Ben / Laura —

Quick internal note before we finalize numbers: I suggest we slightly tighten the recommendation to help procurement move faster: commit to 80 GPUs (instead of 75) to remove one round of re-negotiation if they push for a small buffer, and keep the 50-GPU burst pool. Also propose a 30-day rolling review clause to adjust committed slabs after the first month of telemetry.

Operational asks to include in the SOW:
- Pre-warmed KV cache for scheduled peak windows (we can offer a pre-warm job that runs 15 minutes before predicted spikes)
- A cross-AZ failover playbook with a defined RTO (we usually recommend 5 minutes for DB-backed features; call this out)

If Ben is OK, I’ll update the workbook and draft the procurement blurb.

-Marissa
